purpose: Observed physical scheduler state for the intended 19-role O scheduled-Chat Phase-1 pool. Repository logical enablement and physical scheduler state remain distinct.
cause_evidence: Control10 recorded an exact 19/19 live readback at 17:39:36+09:00. A fresh live scheduler inventory at 18:32:35+09:00 again found 13/19 despite enabled_desired=true for every missing role. Five missing roles recurred from the prior drift set while cross_field remained enabled and integrator newly appeared disabled. Each disabled task's updated_at followed its last_run boundary by about one minute. Same-task re-enable-only updates succeeded and each update response read back is_enabled=true. This strongly localizes the defect to a post-invocation/scheduler-lifecycle boundary, but no evidence proves whether platform lifecycle or a role action caused the disable; do not attribute an actor without direct evidence.

hard_gate.remaining_reason: A third live recurrence proves scheduler persistence remains a Phase-1 blocker. Current-control 19-role execution plus Work-dependency-elimination, zero-residual/zero-quota/cost, rate-limit, conflict/authority/usefulness gates still require durable independent evidence.

readback_policy: Supersede only with a newer live platform inventory. If any intended role stops again, cause-check and re-enable only that same existing enabled_desired task; never lower the 19-role denominator. Preserve exact task last_run/updated_at boundaries and role receipt evidence to distinguish role-requested disable from platform lifecycle disable. Repository file mutation itself does not change physical scheduler state.
